item.title: kb: close the audit gaps
item.description:
Everything the 2026-09-25 audit of `cli/kb-cli`, kb-js, kb-mcp and the Knowledge extension found against `specs/index-api.md` and `specs/index-ui.md`, minus what the single-store change (no `~/.kb`) already fixed.

- The spec was rebuilt from transcripts after the repo loss, so it may have drifted from the original design; check with the user when a ticket leans on a spec detail that looks off.

item.title: kb_get include:["links"] returns no links
item.description:
`kb get D-n --include links --json` emits `links: {outgoing, incoming}` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_get.c`), but kb-js's `readDocumentRead` (`packages/kb-js/src/shape.ts`) never reads it and `KbDocumentRead` has no field for it. So `kb_get` with `include:["links"]` silently returns nothing.

**Done when:** `KbDocumentRead` carries `links?: { outgoing: KbLink[]; incoming: KbLink[] }` exactly when asked for, `readDocumentRead` reads it through the existing `readLink`, and a kb-js contract test against the real binary plus a kb-mcp test cover it.

item.title: Search hits omit scores.fused, and minScore filters raw BM25
item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T in M-3); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

item.title: Knowledge: a document's Refresh button runs a store-wide report
item.description:
The stale badge's refresh action in the document header (`webview/Document.tsx`) sends `{document}`; `src/host.ts` drops it and runs `kb refresh` over the whole store, which only reports and fetches nothing, then silently reloads the tab.

index-ui §3.1 wants a per-document refresh. The honest options: (a) re-read the document's source when it is a file (the locator is its path) and re-file it with `kb add`, (b) for a URL source, re-fetch through the extension's existing `fetchPage`, (c) otherwise say plainly that there is nothing to refresh from. Needs the source route from M-2 only if we want the CLI to own it.

**Done when:** the button refreshes that document (or explains why it cannot), shows the outcome, and never runs a store-wide command.

item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T-11); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S5 (git `6d4a5d0`).

- **`scores.fused`** is on every hit: the reciprocal-rank sum the list is ordered by (1/61 for the top hit of a single list). `vector` stays absent until the vector path runs.
- **`minScore`** stays a floor on the **bm25** score, applied **before** fusion — decided rather than changed. The fused score is 1/(k + rank): it says where a hit landed, not how well it matched (the best hit of a poor query scores the same as the best of a good one), so a floor on it would only be a second `k`. §4 and the code now say so.
- **e2e**: fused present on every hit, 1/61 at the top, hits in fused order; a floor between two hits' bm25 drops only the weaker, and fusion re-ranks the rest from the top. The old test asserted `fused` was absent — it encoded the bug.

Suites: C unit 2296, e2e 141, kb-js 102, kb-mcp 134 — all green; index-vscode 86/87 (only the known T-14 failure).

Left for T-11: kb-js reads an absent `scores.vector` as `0` (`readScores` in `shape.ts`), which blurs the absent-versus-zero distinction the CLI keeps. It only matters once vectors exist.

item.title: Knowledge: opening a search hit does not scroll to its heading in some documents

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S7 (git `bac99b9`).

- **Headings:** the chunk's heading (kept *as written* by the chunker) is brought to the heading *as shown* before its id is made — markdown inline code, emphasis, strikethrough, links, escapes and entities; HTML entities through the HTML renderer's own decoder. **Checked end to end** beyond the unit tests: real `kb` chunks of a markdown, an HTML and a C document, rendered through the real `Body` component (server-side React), all 9 land on an element that exists — before, 4 of the 6 headings and all 3 code chunks would have stayed at the top.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S8 (git `d395dc9`).

- **Log:** `documents.jsonl` gains a `forget` record. The fold drops the document; its id and chunk range stay spent (never reused), links to it read `resolved: false`, and its blob waits for `kb compact`.
- **`kb forget D-n`** forgets one document; **`kb forget S-n`** a source with every document under it. One path (`forget_records`): documents first, then sources, then the keyword index rebuilt, all under one lock.
- **`kb collections delete <name> --with-documents`** forgets what the topic holds. Without the flag it still refuses with `collection_in_use` (now naming the flag) — forgetting a topic's contents is asked for by name. `rename --with-documents` is refused.
- **kb-js:** `forget(id)` → `{documents, sources, note}`, `deleteCollection(name, { withDocuments })`. Not an MCP tool (§9).
- **Knowledge:** a collection's Forget now forgets its documents, as its confirmation already promised, instead of being refused.

**Found and fixed on the way (pre-existing):** kb-js appended `--json` after a `--` separator, where kb read it as a positional — so **renaming or deleting a collection** from Knowledge and **searching for a dash-led query** (from Knowledge or agents) got a text answer kb-js could not parse. `--json` now goes in front of `--`.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 148 (7 new forget tests), kb-js 105 (forget and the collection delete against the real binary, the `--json` placement, key coverage for `forget`), kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green. Spec §7 notes the default refusal.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)
Source routes: sources list/show/refresh, and file ingest

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S9 (git `868092e`).

- **`kb sources [--collection C] [--kind K]`** lists sources; **`kb sources show S-n`** gives the source, its documents, and their **fetch history** (every `document` and `touch` record, oldest first — the fold only keeps the latest, so `doclog_fetches` reads them back).
- **`kb refresh S-n`** reads a **file** source again and re-indexes it only if the text changed (same document id, fresh chunk range). A **url** source is refused with `fetch_failed` (no HTTP client, §12.2 — re-file with `kb add --url`), an **inline** one with `usage` (nothing to read again). `kb refresh` without an id is still §5's report; mixing the two is refused.
- **`refile_document`** is now the one path by which an existing document is handed its text again — `kb add` and `kb refresh S-n` share it (a behaviour-preserving extraction; the whole suite passed before anything was added on top).
- **File ingest by locator** already existed as `kb add --file`; no directory walk, by design (T-12).
- **kb-js:** `sources()`, `source(id)`, `refreshSource(id)`; the key-coverage test checks `sources show` and each `sources` row against what the binary prints.
- **Knowledge:** the `kb:/S-n` page now reads `kb sources show`: kind, locator, last fetch, the documents, the fetch history newest first, and a Refresh action for file sources. Checked rendered in headless Chrome.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 153 (5 new), kb-js 107, kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S10 (git `e80b134`).

- `kb add` is split into **prepare** (kind, locator, mime, hash — refusable before any lock) and **ingest** (write one prepared document), so the single and the batch path are one path. The full suite passed on the restructure before batch was added.
- **`kb add --batch`** reads one JSON object a line on stdin (title, collection, content; url, mime, meta optional). The same locator twice in a batch is one document.
- **kb-js:** `addBatch(documents)`; `readAdded` shared with `add`.
- **kb-mcp:** `kb_add` is one batch call; a refusal returns `filed: 0` and says none were filed. Its description tells agents so. The guard now also forbids `forget` and `refreshSource` from the tools.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S11 (git `a863dd9`).

- **CLI:** errors are `{ok:false, error, message, details?}`. A small `errdet` module holds one pending details object per process, **owned by a code**, so details recorded by a lower layer (the lock in `store_open`, staleness in `fts_open_store`) print only under that code and never ride on an unrelated error.
  - `store_locked` → `{store, pid}`
  - `collection_in_use` → `{collection, documents}`
  - `index_stale` → `{structures: ["keyword"], path}` / `{structures: ["chunks"], document}`; `kb status` carries it inline
  - `fetch_failed` → `{locator}`
  - `unsupported_mime` → `{mime}`: `kb add` (single and batch) now refuses anything not `text/*` or a text-like `application/*` (JSON, XML, YAML, TOML, JS, TS, shell, XHTML), before the store is opened.
  - `model_missing`'s `path` lands with T-10, when the embedder is actually built.
- **kb-js:** `KbError.details` (raw) and `detailsOf(code)`, typed per code in `KbErrorDetails` and shape-checked, so a mis-shaped object reads as null rather than a lie.
- **kb-mcp:** refusals pass `details` to the agent.
- **Knowledge:** delete asks the store first; an empty collection just goes, and one that holds documents is confirmed with the **store's** count from `collection_in_use` — not the row's count from the last refresh.
- **Spec §11** names the fields.

Tests: unit 2319, e2e 158, kb-js 110, kb-mcp 135, index-vscode 96/97 (T-14).

Done in lap session S12 (git `09bf272`). All seven:

- [x] **Source etag/status.** `kb add --etag` (and batch `etag`) records the ETag the caller's fetch saw; a source's `etag` is its newest document's, cleared when new text arrives without one. `status` is recorded: a refresh that cannot read the file marks it `fetch_failed` (once), and the next successful filing sets it back to `ok`. `kb sources --status S --q text`.

Done in lap session S13 (git `07cdcd8`).

- The spec's opening now says kb holds what was **read** (docs, papers, reference source at a pinned version), never the code being **written**, and why: that code is stale as soon as it is indexed, and grep and the LSP already answer it.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S19 (git `3bd227d`).

- **`index/vectors.bin`**: one int8 vector per chunk, keyed by **chunk id**, with the model fingerprint. Chunk ids name one passage forever, so a stored vector stays right as long as the model does:
  - `kb add` and `kb rebuild` embed only chunks with no vector, and drop vectors whose chunks are gone;
  - `kb reindex` re-embeds everything;
  - `rebuild` reports `vectors: {kept, embedded, dropped}`; `reindex` reports the real `reembedded` count.
- **Speed:** a 375-token chunk took **7.3 s**. Two changes brought it to **0.58 s**:
  - `quant_matmul` dequantises each super-block once per sequence instead of once per token (3.6 s);
  - `plat_parallel` (pthreads / Win32) runs the matmul rows and the attention heads on every core.
  - A query takes about 16 ms to embed and about 35 ms end to end.
  - The vectors are **bit-identical** to the old single-threaded pass (hashes compared on three texts), so the llama.cpp comparison still holds.
- **Search:**
  - The default is **hybrid** whenever the store's vectors cover it under the model on disk; otherwise it is keyword, and `mode` in the response says which ran.
  - `--mode hybrid|semantic` refuses with `model_missing`, `model_mismatch`, or `index_stale` on `["vectors"]` with `missing: n`.
  - Both lists go to depth max(3k, 50), then RRF. A chunk found by both paths is one candidate with `matched: ["keyword","semantic"]`.
  - `scores.bm25` and `scores.vector` appear only for the paths that found the hit.
  - Text output shows kw / sem / kw+sem.
- **`kb status`** adds `index.vectors: {count, missing, current}`.
- **kb-js:** `KbScores.bm25` and `.vector` are optional, and `readScores` keeps an absent score absent (the comment on this ticket). One test had pinned the old zeros; it now pins absence.
- **e2e:** `make e2e` picks up the `.gguf` in the real `~/.kb/models` automatically (or `KB_TEST_MODEL`) and skips the model tests without one.
  - The model tests cover: hybrid by default with both scores; semantic ranking the bread note first for a query that shares no word with it; the collection filter; rebuild keeping and dropping vectors; and the missing-vector refusal, keyword fallback and re-embedding.

author: agent
body:
Done: `specs/artifacts.md` (lap session S20).

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S32.

Knowledge already had **Add URL**. It asks before fetching, fetches in the extension host, and files the page as it arrived (HTML is rendered as prose at read time, so the stored bytes stay the page's own). What it lacked, and now has:
- **The ETag.** Add URL files it (`kb add --etag`), so the source records it.
- **Conditional refresh.** A document's Refresh sends `If-None-Match` with the recorded ETag. A **304** re-files the stored text, which only moves `fetchedAt`. A changed page is re-indexed and its new ETag recorded.
- **Url sources.** On a url source's page, Refresh now works: it goes through the same fetch in the extension, since the CLI still has no network, and the answer has the shape the page already shows.
- **Plain failures.** An unreachable host is named with its error code ("Could not reach 127.0.0.1:1: ECONNREFUSED."), and a non-2xx says the status and that **nothing was filed**.

**Test:** a local HTTP server that honours `If-None-Match`, run against the real kb binary. It covers fetch and ETag, an unchanged refresh (with the conditional header checked), a changed page with its new ETag, a 500 that changes nothing, and an unreachable host. index-vscode: 99 pass.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S33.

**Extractor decided: pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist` 6.3, Apache-2.0).** It is pure JavaScript, so there's nothing for the user to install and the vsix stays universal. An external tool like `pdftotext` would be one more thing to set up. It ships as its minified module and worker (1.8 MB) **beside** the bundle and is loaded with a real dynamic import, because it is ES modules that load their worker by relative path. The vsix is now 1.06 MB. Knowledge's dependency guard test names it with the reason, rather than being loosened.

- **Add Files** accepts PDFs. The text is filed as **Markdown**:
  - a `#` title (the PDF's own, or the file name) and its author;
  - one **`## Page N` section per page**, so the heading chunker splits on pages and **a search hit says which page it's on**;
  - lines and paragraphs rebuilt from baselines;
  - prose that would read as Markdown structure escaped.

  The locator is the PDF's path, and the meta records its page count and author.
- **Refresh** on a PDF document reads the file again and re-extracts it.
- **Tests:** 3 new, 102 in total. One takes a hand-built two-page PDF through pdf.js and the real kb binary: search finds page-2 text with heading "Page 2". That test also caught a paragraph-detection bug (upper median of gaps), which is fixed.
- **Checked the packaged vsix:** its pdf.js extracts text without the optional canvas module. The canvas warnings only concern rendering pages as images and will appear in the extension log.

Not done: scanned PDFs (images with no text layer) produce empty pages, because that would need OCR.

item.title: Board: archive
item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

**Design:**
- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.
  - Old readers ignore the new records, and an old writer's whole-item `put` cannot silently un-archive.
  - One file keeps a write atomic under the one lock, and keeps archived ids reserved so they are never reused.
- **Scope:** an item is hidden when it or anything above it (milestone, epic) is archived. Nothing is written to the children, so unarchiving the epic brings everything back.
- **Compatibility:** every existing API and MCP tool keeps its shape. New parameters are optional, the default excludes archived items (which changes nothing until something is archived), and archiving itself is new tools on top.

item.title: Board UI: archive, unarchive, and an Include archived filter
Board: archive
item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

**Design:**
- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.
  - Old readers ignore the new records, and an old writer's whole-item `put` cannot silently un-archive.
  - One file keeps a write atomic under the one lock, and keeps archived ids reserved so they are never reused.
- **Scope:** an item is hidden when it or anything above it (milestone, epic) is archived. Nothing is written to the children, so unarchiving the epic brings everything back.
- **Compatibility:** every existing API and MCP tool keeps its shape. New parameters are optional, the default excludes archived items (which changes nothing until something is archived), and archiving itself is new tools on top.

item.title: kb: ~/.kb (the models folder) is taken for a store, so writes land in the home directory

author: claude
body:
Fixed in lap session S50, git 3cef96a. Nothing under `~` was written by the work or its tests; `~/.kb` still holds only `models/`.

- **Discovery** (`store_is_store`): a `.kb` directory is a store only when it holds `documents.jsonl`. `store_create` has written that since the start, so every real store still qualifies. **The home directory's `.kb` never qualifies**, even with logs planted in it, so the store the bug wrote is not adopted either. Both are walked past, like a plain file named `.kb`. HOME and the directory are compared through `realpath` (new `plat_realpath`), because `HOME` can be a symlink.
- **`kb init` in the home directory** is refused with `init_failed` ("the home directory holds kb's models, not a store").
- **No implicit store:** `kb add` under the home directory, outside any workspace store, answers `not_found` and writes nothing.
- **§1.4** says all of this in words.
